newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka military plane with four aboard missing.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka military plane with four aboard missing.

text.p: A Sri Lankan air force plane with four people aboard was missing over the sea off the northern Jaffna peninsula early on Monday, military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga said.
The navy and air force had launched a search for the aircraft, the spokesman said.
The twin-engined propeller Y-12 aircraft was on a maritime surveillance mission to check a suspected Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) vessel when it lost radio contact, he said.
The Y-12 had taken off at around 4.00 a.m. (2200 GMT) from the Palaly airbase, 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
"The aircraft lost radio contact about 75 miles (120 km) east of Palaly," Jayatunga told Reuters.
Other military officials said the plane was in radio contact with the Palaly airbase until 5.12 a.m. (23:12 GMT).
The Y-12 is a transport aircraft but is often used in surveillance operations to look for rebel arms ships off the north and eastern coasts.

The rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the mainly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island. The government has said more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
